sources: JSC STS-135 Space Shuttle Mission Report: events Appendix A (SRB ignition 189/15:29:03.996; 72% at +38.7, 104.5% at +56.8; both SRMs 50 psia +118.51/118.67; SRB separation command +123.0; 3-g +442.1; MECO MET 8:24; ET sep MET 8:45; OMS assist 83.2 s; OMS-2 TIG MET 37:45, 64.4 s, 97.0 ft/s, 85.2 x 123.9 nmi; SSME Isp tag 451.78 s)

Space Shuttle Missions Summary (NASA 20110001406) STS-135 and App. A: in-plane time 189:15:26:46; max-q 745 (P) / 734 (A) psf; SRB staging 2:02.8 (P) / 2:03.0 (A); FPR 2,821 lb, fuel bias 954 lb; 52 nmi MECO; orbiter 266,050 lb, ET 1,657,525 lb, SRBs 1,298,160 / 1,298,628 lb at SRB ignition
STS-135 Ascent Checklist CC: ASCENT ADI - NOMINAL (the same as STS-134's)
Everything else as sts134-dolilu.json: this flight is flown to test the model built for STS-134
notes: A CROSS-CHECK FLIGHT: the vehicle model and first-stage tables were built for STS-134; STS-135 is flown with them to see which differences from the real flight are the model's.

IYD: the 51.6484-deg plane through the pad at the in-plane time 189:15:26:46 (Missions Summary), its node moved 1.191 deg east -- the offset between that construction and the ISS's own node on STS-134 (322.024 vs 323.215, Space-Track TLE) -- so node 53.132 deg (of date), Earth-fixed at SRB ignition 254.6288 deg.  No STS-135 TLE was available.
Yaw, pitch and roll tables: STS-134's (the same nominal card; the yaw table was built for an in-plane launch, STS-135 launched 2 min 18 s after its in-plane time).
QPOLY at STS-135's throttle times on the simulated vehicle (estimated from STS-134's trajectory, its SRBs 2% faster): T+38.7 and 56.8.

fields.name: PSI(1-30): the tape's 38-deg table turned by -28.71 deg: -18.71 for the inertial azimuth (63.66 -> 44.95), and -10 found by flight -- the first stage then ends 18 nmi out of the final plane instead of 29, the MECO target is reached (-18 and -26 fall short) (PSI = tan(yaw/4), GG31ST.hal step 16)

THET(1,1-30), tan(theta/4): shaped by flight to STS-134's ASCENT ADI - NOMINAL cue card (Ascent Checklist CC 10-11, ASC-14a/134; the same on every OI-34 flight's card): pitch 69/62/52/39/30 deg, H 10/27/51/85/126 kft, Hdot 670/1007/1441/1902/2200 ft/s at T+30/50/70/90/110. Flight p10: 70.1/63.3/56.1/38.9/29.3 deg, 8.9/25.8/49.9/84.3/126.4 kft, 646/1001/1460/1928/2226 ft/s; max-q 716 psf (STS-134: 733.1 at T+60); second stage within ~5 kft of the card from Vi 10,000 on. THET is applied before the yaw turn and load relief takes several degrees at max-q, so it runs well above the flown pitch (to 78.8 deg near Vrel 1,280). Was the tape's table with the pitch-over scaled 0.88 (max-q ~950 psf).
PHI(1-15): the same turn at liftoff (PHI(1) = PSI(1): no roll on the pad), blended out by heads-down 180 deg
QPOLY(1-4): Vrel at STS-135's throttle times T+3.8, 38.7, 56.8 s (estimated)
TREF_ADJUST: estimated time to 488 ft/s (+0.27 s) with STS-135's faster SRBs
GAMD 0.65 deg, as the tape reconfiguration's FPA_NOM (sts134-reconfig.json)

fields.name: IYD_OMS(1): the STS-134 plane (PEG 4 flies the present orbit's plane regardless, GGILTV step 31)
OMS 1: DTIG, HT, THETA, C1, C2 -- the tape's; STS-134 did not need OMS 1 (JSC 37461 Appendix A)
OMS 2: TIG = ET separation + 1,740 s (STS-135: ET sep MET 8:45, OMS-2 TIG MET 37:45); pre-flight targets placeholders -- the ground designs them after MECO for 85.2 x 123.9 nmi
